section_summary: This section covers diplomatic and administrative correspondence concerning reciprocal income tax exemptions for non-diplomatic government officials and employees of the United States and Japan under the Act of August 27, 1935 and Section 116(h) of the Revenue Acts of 1934 and 1936. The Japanese Embassy submitted detailed lists of military attachés, language officers, railway technical experts, monopoly bureau agents, and scientists stationed in the United States to secure Federal income tax exemptions, bond cancellations, and refunds of taxes previously paid. In reciprocal fashion, circular instructions were coordinated across the U.S. State, Treasury, War, Navy, Agriculture, and Commerce Departments directing non-diplomatic American personnel stationed across Japan, Korea (Chosen), and Taiwan to report their tax-exempt incomes directly to local Japanese tax offices annually by March 15. The file also documents the April 1936 official visit to Washington of Japanese Financial Commissioner Yutaro Tomita to discuss international monetary reform, and records the State Department's denial of tax exemption to Iwawo Yokota of the Board of Tourist Industry due to the absence of analogous American public officials abroad.

subfiles.about: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury confirms that certified Japanese government officials in New York are exempt from Federal income tax.
subfiles.from: Wayne Taylor, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Concluding page of a Treasury Department letter quoting statutory provisions governing reciprocal tax exemption for foreign government personnel. It lists Japanese officials stationed in New York belonging to the Navy Department, Railway Department, Finance Department (Tobacco Monopoly Bureau and Financial Commissioner), and War Department. In view of Under Secretary William Phillips' certification, the officials are confirmed exempt from Federal income tax on their official salaries, and the local collector of internal revenue is to be notified.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State regarding Tax Exemption for Japanese Officials

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State informs the Japanese Ambassador that Japanese officials on the March 14 list have been granted income tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: The Department of State refers to the Japanese Ambassador's note of March 14, 1936, transmitting a list of Japanese government officials residing in the United States seeking tax exemption. The note informs the Ambassador that the U.S. Treasury has confirmed their exempt status on salaries received as compensation for official services. It adds that the Collector of Internal Revenue for the district in which their offices are situated will be advised accordingly.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Income Tax Exemption for Japanese Officials

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms tax exemption for an additional list of Japanese military, forestry, and Formosan government officials.
subfiles.from: Wayne Taylor, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: In response to State Department communications under Public Act No. 374, the Acting Secretary of the Treasury reviews an additional list of Japanese officials. The list includes seventeen naval officers, three Raw Silk Intelligence Bureau officials, one Formosa Government commissioner, and thirteen naval and army officers stationed outside New York. Treasury holds them exempt from Federal income tax and notes that collectors at New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Seattle will be instructed to issue certificates of compliance upon their departure.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State regarding Additional Japanese Officials Exempt from Taxation

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State notifies the Japanese Ambassador of tax exemption and instructions sent to major port collectors.
subfiles.summary: Referring to Embassy note No. 54 of March 19, 1936, the Secretary of State informs the Japanese Ambassador that the Treasury Department has granted Federal income tax exemption to the officials listed therein. Collectors of internal revenue for the districts where they reside will be instructed accordingly. Furthermore, the collectors at the ports of New York City, Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Seattle will be notified so the officials may obtain departure certificates of compliance without inconvenience.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Tax Exemption and Clearance at Ports

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department acknowledges a Japanese request for future tax exemptions, cancellation of surety bonds, and tax refunds.
subfiles.from: Wayne Taylor, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the State Department's letter of April 8, 1936, which transmitted a note from the Japanese Ambassador dated March 19, 1936. The note submitted an additional list of Japanese officials seeking future tax exemption, cancellation of deposited surety bonds, and refund of income taxes paid in the past. Treasury states that careful consideration will be given and a formal reply provided at the earliest practicable date.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State acknowledging Request for Tax Refunds and Bond Cancellations

subfiles.about: Records a telephone conversation regarding the upcoming April visit to Washington of Japanese Financial Commissioner Yutaro Tomita.
subfiles.from: William T. Turner, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Katsuo Okazaki of the Japanese Embassy informed William T. Turner by telephone that Yutaro Tomita, Financial Commissioner to the United States and Great Britain, would visit Washington in late April to confer on international finance and currency issues. Okazaki noted that Tomita carries the rank of vice minister of finance and would likely seek a meeting with the Secretary of the Treasury. State Department comments note Tomita's succession to Juichi Tsushima and suggest ascertaining whether Tomita has concrete proposals to offer before his arrival.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation between Katsuo Okazaki and William T. Turner regarding Visit of Yutaro Tomita

subfiles.about: Provides biographical background on Financial Commissioner Yutaro Tomita and reviews the historical role of the Japanese Financial Commission.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman and William T. Turner, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Prepared for Under Secretary William Phillips prior to Tomita's visit, the memorandum traces Tomita's official career in the Japanese Finance Department and the Bank of Japan, his appointment in 1934, and his participation in the 1921 Washington Conference. It analyzes the role of the Financial Commissioner in London, Paris, and New York, contrasting historical loan-floating operations during the Russo-Japanese War under Korekiyo Takahashi with contemporary functions involving bond repurchases and liaison with the Yokohama Specie Bank.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Yutaro Tomita, Financial Commissioner of the Japanese Government
subfiles.to: Under Secretary of State William Phillips

subfiles.about: Duplicate carbon copy of the biographical and analytical memorandum concerning Japanese Financial Commissioner Yutaro Tomita.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman and William T. Turner, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Identical file copy of the April 21, 1936 memorandum detailing the career background of Financial Commissioner Yutaro Tomita ahead of his conference with Under Secretary Phillips and Secretary Hull. It reviews the historical evolution of the Financial Commissioner's office abroad, noting the flotation of foreign loans during the Russo-Japanese War and modern bond purchases. This copy is stamped as received by the Office of the Under Secretary of State.
subfiles.title: Duplicate Memorandum on Yutaro Tomita, Financial Commissioner of the Japanese Government
subfiles.to: Under Secretary of State William Phillips

subfiles.about: Suggests asking the Japanese Embassy to explain the specific duties of Iwawo Yokota to assess eligibility for tax exemption.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Dooman notes that the Department had previously informed the Japanese Embassy that Mr. Yokota could not be granted tax exemption because the U.S. Government maintains no officers abroad performing analogous duties. Observing that the Japanese Embassy's latest note implicitly seeks reconsideration of Yokota's case, Dooman asks Miss Marsh whether the Department should request a detailed explanation of Yokota's official duties.
subfiles.title: Internal Memorandum from Eugene H. Dooman to Miss Marsh regarding the Case of Iwawo Yokota
subfiles.to: Miss Marsh, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: Clarifies that Iwawo Yokota is Secretary of the Board of Tourist Industry of the Japanese Government Railways, distinct from the private Japan Tourist Bureau.
subfiles.summary: With reference to note No. 68 of April 15, 1936, the Japanese Ambassador states that the official title of Mr. Iwawo Yokota is Secretary of the Board of Tourist Industry of the Japanese Government Railways, rather than Secretary of the Tourist Bureau. The Ambassador emphasizes that the Board is an official governmental entity expressly distinguished from the Japan Tourist Bureau, which was established as a separate juridical person.
subfiles.title: Note No. 104 from the Japanese Ambassador to the Secretary of State regarding Title of Iwawo Yokota

subfiles.about: Requests a detailed explanation of the duties performed by Iwawo Yokota with a view to further consideration of his tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges note No. 104 of May 14, 1936, regarding the corrected title of Mr. Iwawo Yokota as Secretary of the Board of Tourist Industry of the Japanese Government Railways. In order to give further consideration to the request for exemption from income taxation on his official salary, the Secretary asks the Ambassador to furnish a detailed explanation of the character of Mr. Yokota's duties.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador requesting Details on Iwawo Yokota's Duties

subfiles.about: Requests income tax exemption for Kyoichi Suzuki, Ryokichi Sagane, and Osamu Tsubota.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests that three Japanese officials staying in the United States be added to the exemption list attached to note No. 50 of March 14, 1936. The officials are Kyoichi Suzuki (Communications Department, New York), studying non-rail communications; Ryokichi Sagane (assistant professor at Tokyo Imperial University, Berkeley), conducting physical research; and Osamu Tsubota (Government Railways, Washington, D.C.), studying railway and transportation systems.
subfiles.title: Note No. 106 from the Japanese Ambassador to the Secretary of State requesting Tax Exemption for Three Officials

subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese note No. 106 and certifies reciprocity under Public Act No. 374 for Suzuki, Sagane, and Tsubota.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr., a copy of note No. 106 from the Japanese Ambassador requesting tax exemption for three Japanese officials. Hull certifies under the Act of August 27, 1935, that Japan grants equivalent tax exemption to American personnel and that the services performed are similar in character. He requests that exemption be granted and that interested Treasury officers be notified.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury certifying Reciprocity for Three Japanese Officials
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of note No. 106 and states that the request for tax exemption has been referred to the Treasury.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges note No. 106 of May 15, 1936, containing an additional list of three Japanese officials residing in the United States. The note informs the Japanese Ambassador that their names have been forwarded to the appropriate federal authorities with a view to favorable action, and that a further communication will be addressed to the Ambassador upon receipt of a reply.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador acknowledging Note No. 106

subfiles.about: Advises that American officials in Japan should report their tax-exempt incomes directly to local tax offices by March 15 annually.
subfiles.summary: Referring to note No. 60 of March 31, 1936, the Japanese Ambassador informs the Secretary of State that the Japanese Department of Finance does not require a special list of American officials through the American Embassy in Tokyo. To facilitate exemption, American officials residing in Japan should instead report their names, official titles, and tax-exempt incomes directly to local Japanese tax offices annually by March 15. The Ambassador asks that this desire be notified to the American authorities concerned.
subfiles.title: Note No. 115 from the Japanese Ambassador to the Secretary of State on Tax Reporting Procedures in Japan

subfiles.about: Clarifies that the annual tax reporting procedure in note No. 115 applies only to non-diplomatic American personnel.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador presents his compliments to the Secretary of State to clarify that the American officials referred to in note No. 115 of May 22, 1936, do not include diplomatic and consular officials of the American Government residing in Japan. Consequently, the local March 15 tax filing instruction applies exclusively to non-diplomatic staff and employees.
subfiles.title: Note No. 118 from the Japanese Ambassador to the Secretary of State clarifying Scope of American Officials Covered

subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese notes Nos. 115 and 118 regarding annual tax reporting for non-diplomatic American personnel in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State encloses copies of Japanese Embassy notes Nos. 115 and 118 for the information and action of the Treasury Department. Treasury is informed that American officials and employees, other than diplomatic and consular officers, residing in Japan must report their names, official titles, and tax-exempt salaries to local Japanese tax offices by March 15 annually to obtain tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury transmitting Japanese Notes on Tax Reporting

subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese notes on tax reporting to the War Department for personnel stationed in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State forwards copies of notes Nos. 115 and 118 from the Japanese Ambassador to the Secretary of War. The letter advises that non-diplomatic American personnel stationed in Japan, including War Department employees, must submit annual reports of their tax-exempt incomes directly to local Japanese tax offices by March 15.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of War transmitting Japanese Notes on Tax Reporting

subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese notes on tax reporting to the Navy Department for personnel stationed in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits copies of Japanese notes Nos. 115 and 118 to the Secretary of the Navy. Navy Department employees and non-diplomatic officers stationed in Japan are notified that they must report their names, titles, and tax-exempt compensation to local Japanese tax authorities by March 15 annually to maintain tax-exempt status.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Navy transmitting Japanese Notes on Tax Reporting

subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese notes on tax reporting to the Commerce Department for personnel stationed in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State sends copies of Japanese notes Nos. 115 and 118 to the Secretary of Commerce. The communication explains that Commerce Department employees and non-diplomatic representatives in Japan must report their official salaries to local tax offices by March 15 each year to obtain exemption from Japanese income taxation.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of Commerce transmitting Japanese Notes on Tax Reporting

subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese notes on tax reporting to the Department of Agriculture for personnel stationed in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits copies of Japanese notes Nos. 115 and 118 to the Secretary of Agriculture. Agriculture Department staff and employees residing in Japan are instructed to report their names, official titles, and exempt salaries to local Japanese tax offices by March 15 annually to claim income tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of Agriculture transmitting Japanese Notes on Tax Reporting

subfiles.about: Instructs the Tokyo consulate on the annual tax reporting procedure for American non-diplomatic personnel.
subfiles.summary: Circular instruction to the American Consular Officer in charge at Tokyo enclosing Japanese Embassy notes Nos. 115 and 118. Non-diplomatic American officials and employees residing in Japan must report their tax-exempt incomes directly to local Japanese tax offices by March 15 annually. It notes that similar instructions were sent to the Embassy at Tokyo, other consulates in Japan, and relevant Washington departments.
subfiles.title: Instruction from the Secretary of State to the American Consular Officer in Charge at Tokyo
subfiles.to: The American Consular Officer in charge, Tokyo, Japan

subfiles.about: Directs the Kobe consulate to instruct non-diplomatic staff to file annual tax reports by March 15.
subfiles.summary: Identical circular instruction transmitting copies of Japanese notes Nos. 115 and 118 to the American Consulate at Kobe. Consular personnel classified as non-diplomatic employees must file annual tax-exempt income reports with local Japanese tax offices by March 15. The circular notes identical distribution to the embassy and all consulates across the Japanese Empire.
subfiles.title: Instruction from the Secretary of State to the American Consular Officer in Charge at Kobe
subfiles.to: The American Consular Officer in charge, Kobe, Japan

subfiles.about: Directs the Nagoya consulate regarding the annual March 15 tax exemption procedure for American employees.
subfiles.summary: Circular instruction to the American Consular Officer in charge at Nagoya enclosing Japanese Embassy notes Nos. 115 and 118. American non-diplomatic officials and employees residing in Japan are instructed to report their names, titles, and tax-exempt incomes to local tax authorities by March 15 annually to secure exemption from Japanese income tax.
subfiles.title: Instruction from the Secretary of State to the American Consular Officer in Charge at Nagoya
subfiles.to: The American Consular Officer in charge, Nagoya, Japan

subfiles.about: Instructs the Yokohama consulate regarding local reporting by March 15 for Japanese tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: Circular instruction transmitting notes Nos. 115 and 118 from the Japanese Ambassador to the American Consulate at Yokohama. Consular employees and other non-diplomatic American personnel are instructed to report annually by March 15 to local Japanese tax offices to secure exemption from Japanese income taxation.
subfiles.title: Instruction from the Secretary of State to the American Consular Officer in Charge at Yokohama
subfiles.to: The American Consular Officer in charge, Yokohama, Japan

subfiles.about: Directs the Taihoku consulate in Taiwan regarding tax exemption reporting for American employees.
subfiles.summary: Circular instruction to the American Consular Officer in charge at Taihoku, Taiwan, transmitting Japanese notes Nos. 115 and 118. Non-diplomatic American personnel stationed in Taiwan are instructed to report their official salaries to local tax offices by March 15 annually to claim Japanese income tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Instruction from the Secretary of State to the American Consular Officer in Charge at Taihoku
subfiles.to: The American Consular Officer in charge, Taihoku, Taiwan

subfiles.about: Directs the Seoul consulate in Korea regarding tax exemption reporting for American employees.
subfiles.summary: Circular instruction to the American Consular Officer in charge at Seoul, Chosen (Korea), enclosing copies of Japanese Embassy notes Nos. 115 and 118. American non-diplomatic personnel stationed in Korea must report their names, titles, and tax-exempt compensation to local Japanese tax authorities by March 15 each year.
subfiles.title: Instruction from the Secretary of State to the American Consular Officer in Charge at Seoul
subfiles.to: The American Consular Officer in charge, Seoul, Chosen

subfiles.about: Instructs the Tokyo embassy regarding annual tax reporting for non-diplomatic American personnel in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 1057 transmits copies of Japanese notes Nos. 115 and 118 to the American Ambassador in Tokyo. It directs that all American non-diplomatic personnel and employees in Japan report their incomes to local tax offices by March 15 annually to claim income tax exemption, noting that identical instructions were sent to all U.S. consulates in Japan and relevant Washington departments.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 1057 from the Secretary of State to the American Ambassador at Tokyo

subfiles.about: Informs the Japanese Ambassador that instructions on tax reporting have been sent to U.S. missions in Japan and domestic departments.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy notes Nos. 115 and 118 concerning the March 15 tax reporting procedure for American non-diplomatic personnel in Japan. He confirms that copies of both notes have been transmitted to the American Embassy at Tokyo, all American consular offices in Japan, and all U.S. Government departments with personnel stationed in Japan.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Action Taken on Notes Nos. 115 and 118

subfiles.about: Confirms the cancellation of surety bonds, abatement of assessments, and filing of refund claims for Japanese officials.
subfiles.from: Wayne Taylor, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Referring to notes from the Japanese Ambassador dated March 21 and March 31, 1936, the Acting Secretary of the Treasury confirms that Japanese railway, navy, army, and Formosan officials are exempt from Federal income tax. The internal revenue collector will be instructed to abate assessments against officials who deposited surety bonds, release the surety company from liability, and invite officials who paid taxes to submit claims for refund.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State regarding Tax Abatements and Refund Claims

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting a Treasury conference with Yutaro Tomita regarding the financial situation in China.
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference note indexing a memorandum filed under decimal file 893.515/1100 concerning a conference on Chinese monetary reform. The conference took place between the Secretary of the Treasury and Japanese Financial Commissioner Yutaro Tomita, attended also by the Japanese Ambassador, the Assistant Financial Attaché, and Stanley K. Hornbeck.
subfiles.title: Document File Note regarding Conference on Chinese Monetary Reform and Yutaro Tomita

subfiles.about: Requests tax exemption for two Japanese Army language officers and four railway technical experts in New York.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption for six Japanese officials temporarily sojourning in New York. The officials comprise Lieutenant Colonel Torashiro Asano and Major Tomojiro Honda, army language officers studying the American language, and Shuichiro Sato, Kazutoshi Nakashima, Seiichi Ogawa, and Seiichi Hayashi, technical experts studying railway systems and inspecting materials purchased for the Japanese Government Railways.
subfiles.title: Note No. 128 from the Japanese Ambassador to the Secretary of State requesting Tax Exemption for Six Officials

subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese note No. 128 and certifies reciprocal tax exemption for two army officers and four railway experts.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits a copy of note No. 128 from the Japanese Ambassador to the Secretary of the Treasury. In accordance with the Act of August 27, 1935, Hull certifies that Japan grants equivalent tax exemption to American personnel performing similar functions in Japan and requests that the Treasury grant income tax exemption to the six Japanese army officers and railway technical experts stationed in New York.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury certifying Reciprocity for Six Japanese Officials
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of note No. 128 regarding six Japanese officials and notes referral to the Treasury Department.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges note No. 128 of June 17, 1936, listing Japanese officials on temporary duty in the United States seeking tax exemption. The note informs the Ambassador that the matter has been submitted to the appropriate federal authorities for decision, with a further communication to follow upon receiving their reply.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador acknowledging Note No. 128

subfiles.about: Confirms that the Treasury Department has granted tax exemption to the two army officers and four railway experts in New York.
subfiles.summary: Referring to note No. 128 of June 17, 1936, the Secretary of State informs the Japanese Ambassador that the competent U.S. authority (Treasury Department) has ruled that the six Japanese army officers and railway technical experts are exempt from Federal income tax on their official salaries. The appropriate collectors of internal revenue will be notified accordingly.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador confirming Tax Exemption for Six Officials

subfiles.about: Confirms notification to the American Commercial Attaché in Tokyo regarding Japanese tax-exemption reporting.
subfiles.from: Lacey C. Zapf, Liaison Officer, Department of Commerce
subfiles.summary: Lacey C. Zapf, Liaison Officer of the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce, acknowledges receipt of State Department memorandum FA 894.01B 11/62 regarding tax-exempt incomes of American non-diplomatic personnel in Japan. He confirms that appropriate notice has been forwarded to the office of the American Commercial Attaché in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Department of Commerce to Assistant Secretary of State Wilbur J. Carr
subfiles.to: Wilbur J. Carr, Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Holds that Kyoichi Suzuki, Ryokichi Sagane, and Osamu Tsubota are exempt from Federal income tax.
subfiles.from: Josephine Roche, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: In response to the State Department's letter of May 21, 1936, Acting Secretary of the Treasury Josephine Roche confirms that in view of State Department certification under the Act of August 27, 1935 (Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1934), the Japanese officials Kyoichi Suzuki, Ryokichi Sagane, and Osamu Tsubota are exempt from Federal income tax on their official salaries. Collectors of internal revenue will be advised accordingly.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of the Treasury Josephine Roche to the Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Transmits an excerpt from the Treasury Department confirming tax exemption for Suzuki, Sagane, and Tsubota.
subfiles.summary: Referring to Embassy note No. 106 of May 15, 1936, the Secretary of State informs the Japanese Ambassador that the Treasury Department has granted income tax exemption to Kyoichi Suzuki, Ryokichi Sagane, and Osamu Tsubota. An excerpt from the Treasury letter of June 18, 1936, is enclosed, and the Ambassador is assured that relevant collectors of internal revenue will be notified.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador enclosing Excerpt of Treasury Letter

subfiles.about: Reports that the Military Attaché in Tokyo has been instructed regarding Japanese tax exemption procedures.
subfiles.from: Malin Craig, Chief of Staff, War Department
subfiles.summary: General Malin Craig, Chief of Staff, acknowledges on behalf of the Secretary of War the State Department's letter of June 13, 1936 (FA 894.01B 11/62). He reports that the Military Attaché at the American Embassy in Tokyo has been informed and directed to advise all military personnel under his jurisdiction regarding the procedure for claiming Japanese income tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Letter from Chief of Staff Malin Craig to the Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Acknowledges State Department communication regarding tax exemption procedures for Treasury personnel in Japan.
subfiles.from: Wm. H. McReynolds, Administrative Assistant to the Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Writing by direction of the Secretary of the Treasury, Wm. H. McReynolds acknowledges receipt of the State Department's letter of June 13, 1936, which transmitted notes Nos. 115 and 118 from the Japanese Ambassador. He confirms that the instructions regarding tax exemption for American Treasury officials and employees residing in Japan have been brought to the attention of the appropriate Treasury officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from Administrative Assistant Wm. H. McReynolds to the Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Requests expedited tax exemption for Daisuke Kanetomo prior to his departure on the S.S. Aquitania.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax-exempt status for Mr. Daisuke Kanetomo, technical expert of the Japanese Department of Agriculture and Forestry, residing in Los Angeles to study the U.S. fishery industry. Noting that Kanetomo is scheduled to depart New York for Europe on the steamship Aquitania on July 16, the Ambassador urges immediate notification to New York tax authorities to ensure timely exemption and departure clearance.
subfiles.title: Note No. 138 from the Japanese Ambassador to the Secretary of State regarding Daisuke Kanetomo

subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese note No. 138, certifies reciprocity for Daisuke Kanetomo, and requests urgent clearance.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits Japanese note No. 138 requesting tax exemption for Daisuke Kanetomo under Public Act No. 374. Hull certifies that Japan extends reciprocal exemptions to American personnel and requests prompt Treasury approval, highlighting Kanetomo's impending departure from New York on July 16 aboard the S.S. Aquitania.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury certifying Reciprocity for Daisuke Kanetomo
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Recommends denying tax exemption to Iwawo Yokota because his tourist promotion activities lack a U.S. counterpart.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum notes that the Japanese Embassy mistakenly presumes government employment automatically confers tax exemption under U.S. law. It observes that Yokota's tourist promotion duties belong to a commercial field handled by private initiative in most countries, including the United States. Concluding that certifying reciprocity would unduly stretch the statute since the U.S. Government maintains no analogous officers abroad, the memorandum recommends informing the Japanese Embassy that State cannot issue the required certificate.
subfiles.title: Internal Memorandum to Miss Marsh regarding Iwawo Yokota's Eligibility for Tax Exemption
subfiles.to: Miss Marsh, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: Queries whether the United States employs any officials abroad performing duties similar to Iwawo Yokota.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten note from the Office of the Legal Adviser asking Far Eastern Affairs whether the U.S. Government maintains officers in foreign countries whose duties are analogous to those of Mr. Iwawo Yokota. It also queries whether it is pertinent to consider the functions performed by other officials of the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Note from the Office of the Legal Adviser to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: Notes requirements regarding sufficient information before Japanese officials in the U.S. are certified for tax exemption.
subfiles.from: William R. Vallance, Office of the Legal Adviser
subfiles.summary: Brief handwritten note by Assistant Legal Adviser William R. Vallance concerning the criteria for exempting Japanese officials staying in the United States from taxation. It emphasizes the necessity of having sufficient information regarding their status and official functions to ensure they are properly certified.
subfiles.title: Internal Note by William R. Vallance on Japanese Officials' Tax Exemption

subfiles.about: Submits an official explanation from the Japanese Railways Department regarding the governmental duties of Iwawo Yokota.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador encloses an excerpt dated May 23, 1936, from the Japanese Government Railways explaining that the State Department has confused Mr. Yokota's role with private tourist agencies. The explanation states that the Board of Tourist Industry is an executive government organ supervising private bodies (Japan Tourist Bureau and Japan Travel Publicity Association), and that Yokota was ordered by the Minister of Railways to study tourist promotion systems and supervise these associations in Los Angeles and New York. The Ambassador requests that Yokota be accorded the same tax-exempt treatment as other Japanese railway officials.
subfiles.title: Note No. 143 from the Japanese Ambassador to the Secretary of State regarding Iwawo Yokota, with Enclosure

subfiles.about: Formally declines to certify tax exemption for Iwawo Yokota due to the lack of an equivalent American office.
subfiles.summary: Referring to note No. 143 of July 7, 1936, the Secretary of State regrets to inform the Japanese Ambassador that tax exemption cannot be granted to Mr. Iwawo Yokota, Secretary of the Board of Tourist Industry. The note explains that because the United States Government maintains no officers abroad performing duties analogous to those of Mr. Yokota, the State Department cannot issue the certificate of reciprocity required under Public Act No. 374.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador denying Tax Exemption for Iwawo Yokota

subfiles.about: Submits an additional list of Japanese officials who paid U.S. income taxes and requests refunds.
subfiles.summary: Referring to note No. 55 of March 21, 1936, the Japanese Ambassador encloses a list of three Japanese officials who paid federal income taxes to collectors in New York and Los Angeles. The list details payments by Hisao Okabayashi ($23.11, Tobacco Monopoly Bureau), Takeshi Takei ($3.67, Tokyo Industrial University), and Katsuji Tanaka ($91.84, Navy Department) covering years 1932 to 1935. The Ambassador asks that the list be forwarded to the appropriate authorities so that the amounts paid may be refunded.
subfiles.title: Note No. 149 from the Japanese Ambassador to the Secretary of State requesting Tax Refunds, with Enclosure

subfiles.about: Analyzes the legal necessity of establishing the exact effective date of Japanese tax exemption to evaluate refund claims.
subfiles.from: William T. Turner, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Turner notes that the Japanese Embassy's request for refunds of taxes paid by Japanese officials extends back to 1932. Because the U.S. statute authorizes tax exemption only on a basis of reciprocal treatment, Turner explains that the precise date on which Japan made effective its exemption for American officials must be determined. Assistant Legal Adviser William R. Vallance approved the draft inquiry to the Japanese Embassy.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by William T. Turner on Tax Refund Requests dating back to 1932

subfiles.about: Asks the Japanese Ambassador to specify the date when Japanese exemption for U.S. officials became effective.
subfiles.summary: Referring to note No. 55 of March 21, 1936, which stated that Japanese internal revenue officers had been instructed to exempt all U.S. Government officials from income taxation, the Secretary of State requests clarification. To determine the retroactive validity of refund claims, the Secretary asks to be informed of the exact date on which the Japanese exemption was made effective.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador inquiring about Effective Date of Japanese Exemption

subfiles.about: Brief internal note concerning correspondence on tax exemption for officials in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Fragmentary internal office slip from the Office of the Legal Adviser noting correspondence regarding tax exemption matters relating to officials in Japan. The slip accompanied internal departmental circulation of the tax exemption files.
subfiles.title: Internal Routing Slip of the Legal Adviser

subfiles.about: Confirms that Daisuke Kanetomo is exempt from Federal income tax under the Revenue Act.
subfiles.from: Wayne C. Taylor, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: In response to the State Department's letter of July 8, 1936, Acting Secretary of the Treasury Wayne C. Taylor acknowledges receipt of Japanese note No. 138. In view of State Department certification, the Treasury holds that Daisuke Kanetomo is exempt from Federal income tax on his official compensation, and internal revenue collectors have been notified. Taylor notes that the provisions of Public Act No. 374 have been codified as Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1936.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State regarding Daisuke Kanetomo

subfiles.about: Confirms telephonic notice that Daisuke Kanetomo has been granted Federal income tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: Referring to note No. 138 of July 2, 1936, the Secretary of State confirms a telephone communication made to the Japanese Embassy stating that Daisuke Kanetomo has been held exempt from Federal income tax. The note states that the competent U.S. authorities have advised the appropriate collectors of internal revenue, facilitating Kanetomo's departure.
subfiles.title: Note from the Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador confirming Tax Exemption for Daisuke Kanetomo

subfiles.about: Confirms Federal income tax exemption for the six Japanese army officers and railway experts in New York.
subfiles.from: Wayne C. Taylor, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: In response to the State Department's letter of June 20, 1936, the Acting Secretary of the Treasury rules that the six Japanese officials named in note No. 128 (Asano, Honda, Sato, Nakashima, Ogawa, and Hayashi) are exempt from Federal income tax. Collectors of internal revenue will be notified, and it is noted that these exemption rules are now codified under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1936.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State regarding Six Japanese Officials

subfiles.about: Short internal note regarding the handling of Japanese tax exemption correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Brief handwritten note from the Legal Adviser's office addressed to Mr. Turner of Far Eastern Affairs concerning tax exemption documentation and procedure.
subfiles.title: Internal Note from the Office of the Legal Adviser to William T. Turner
subfiles.to: William T. Turner, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: Raises question about discrepancies in the dates of stay of Japanese officials seeking tax refunds.
subfiles.summary: An official in Foreign Service Administration writes to Assistant Legal Adviser William R. Vallance noting that the recorded periods of stay in the United States for Japanese officials seeking tax refunds do not match previous records. The note queries whether the Department will need to request a clarifying statement from the Japanese Ambassador each time new lists are submitted.
subfiles.title: Internal Memorandum to William R. Vallance regarding Discrepancies in Length of Stay
subfiles.to: William R. Vallance, Office of the Legal Adviser

subfiles.about: Transmits note No. 149 and certifies reciprocity to support income tax refunds for Okabayashi, Takei, and Tanaka.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull writes to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr., pursuant to Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1936. Hull transmits note No. 149 from the Japanese Ambassador and certifies that Japan grants equivalent tax exemptions to American personnel and that the services performed are analogous. He requests that future compensation of the three officials be exempt, that past income taxes paid to collectors in New York and Los Angeles be refunded, and that internal revenue officers be instructed accordingly.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury regarding Tax Refunds for Three Japanese Officials
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Reports that the Embassy has asked Tokyo for the exact effective date of Japan's tax exemption for U.S. officials.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador acknowledges receipt of the Secretary of State's note dated July 22, 1936, inquiring as to the effective date of the Japanese tax exemption. The Ambassador reports that he has cabled Tokyo to ascertain the exact date on which the exemption mentioned in note No. 55 took effect, and promises to communicate the information as soon as a reply is received. Page 239 is a duplicate carbon copy of the note.
subfiles.title: Note No. 154 from the Japanese Ambassador to the Secretary of State regarding Effective Date Inquiry

subfiles.about: Reports that American employees at the Yokohama consulate have been instructed on claiming Japanese tax exemption.
subfiles.from: Gregor C. Merrill, American Vice Consul, Yokohama
subfiles.summary: Vice Consul Gregor C. Merrill reports that following consultation with the Consul General at Tokyo, the contents of State Department instruction of June 13, 1936 (File No. 894.01B 11/62) were communicated to the four American employees at the Yokohama consulate. The employees have been directed to report their incomes to the local Japanese tax authorities annually on March 15 to claim tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 887 from American Vice Consul Gregor C. Merrill to the Secretary of State
